dialect.label: Fagor 8060 / 8065
dialect.about: Fagor's current control. Its own language: ; comments to the end of the line, $ and # statements, %L local subroutines, P parameters (XP1), G70/G71 units, tool length from D, and drilling cycles where Z is the reference plane and I the depth.

G43.text: Fagor 8060/8065 has no G43. The tool length offset comes from D (D1 on, D0 off) and applies on the next move along the tool axis.

G44.text: Fagor 8060/8065 has no G44. The tool length offset comes from D (D0 cancels it).

G49.text: Fagor 8060/8065 has no G49. D0 cancels the tool length offset.

G21.text: Fagor has no G21. Millimeters are G71 (inch is G70); G20 sets the plane.

G28.text: Fagor 8060/8065 has no G28 home return; G74 is the home search.

G65.text: Fagor has no G65 macro call. Call a subroutine with #CALL or #PCALL, or LL for a local one.

G76.text: Fagor 8060/8065 has no G76. Boring is G86.

G89.text: On a Fagor mill G89 isn't a cycle. Bore with a dwell is G86 with K.

M98.text: Fagor has no M98. Call a subroutine with #CALL name (or LL name for a local %L subroutine).

M99.text: Fagor ends a subroutine with M17, M29 or #RET, not M99.

M98.text: The Fagor 8060/8065 has no M98. Call a subroutine with #CALL, or a local one with LL.

M99.text: The Fagor 8060/8065 ends a subroutine with M17, M29 or #RET, not M99.

G80.text: The Fagor 8060/8065 lathe has no G80: its cycles aren't modal, so there's nothing to cancel.

G98.text: On the Fagor 8060/8065 lathe, G94 is feed per minute; G98 is a mill cycle code.

G99.text: On the Fagor 8060/8065 lathe, G95 is feed per rev; G99 is a mill cycle code.

G43.text: The Fagor 8060/8065 has no G43: the tool's D offset applies its length.

G50.text: On the Fagor 8060/8065, G50 is a semi-rounded corner, not a speed limit. Limit the spindle speed with G192 S.

G66.about: Roughs by repeating the profile until the stock I is gone, then finishes at feed H. The profile is in this program between labels S and E, in local subroutine P (E and S then ignored), in global subroutine Q, or between labels S and E in global subroutine Q. After the cycle G00, G40 and G90 are active.

A: Main direction: A0 along Z, A1 along X.
M: Finish stock in Z. Left out, it equals L.
H: Finish pass feed. None or 0: no finish pass.
S: Label of the first line of the profile. Not used with P.
E: Label of the last line of the profile. Not used with P.
P: Local subroutine that holds the whole profile; S and E are then ignored.
Q: Global subroutine that holds the profile, alone or with S and E.

G68.about: Roughs along X following the profile. The profile is in this program between labels S and E, in local subroutine P (E and S then ignored), in global subroutine Q, or between labels S and E in global subroutine Q. After the cycle G00, G40 and G90 are active.

D: Safety distance. D0 keeps the tool on the profile between passes; left out, it climbs the profile.
M: Finish stock in Z. Left out, it equals L.
H: Finish pass feed. None or 0: no finish pass.
F: Feed for the last roughing pass.
S: Label of the first line of the profile. Not used with P.
E: Label of the last line of the profile. Not used with P.
P: Local subroutine that holds the whole profile; S and E are then ignored.
Q: Global subroutine that holds the profile, alone or with S and E.

G69.about: Roughs along Z following the profile. The profile is in this program between labels S and E, in local subroutine P (E and S then ignored), in global subroutine Q, or between labels S and E in global subroutine Q. After the cycle G00, G40 and G90 are active.

D: Safety distance. D0 keeps the tool on the profile between passes; left out, it climbs the profile.
M: Finish stock in Z. Left out, it equals L.
H: Finish pass feed. None or 0: no finish pass.
F: Feed for the last roughing pass.
S: Label of the first line of the profile. Not used with P.
E: Label of the last line of the profile. Not used with P.
P: Local subroutine that holds the whole profile; S and E are then ignored.
Q: Global subroutine that holds the profile, alone or with S and E.

G81.about: Straight turning from X Z to Q R in passes of C.

D: Safety distance. D0 or left out: the tool goes back along the profile.
M: Finish stock in Z. Left out, 0.
H: Finish pass feed. None or 0: no finish pass.
F: Feed for the last roughing pass.

G82.about: Straight facing from X Z to Q R in passes of C.

D: Safety distance. D0 or left out: the tool goes back along the profile.
M: Finish stock in Z. Left out, 0.
H: Finish pass feed. None or 0: no finish pass.
F: Feed for the last roughing pass.

G83.about: Drilling (B is the peck) or tapping (B0) along Z at X Z, to depth I. The tool ends at the approach point and G40 is active after the cycle.

K: Dwell at the bottom, in hundredths of a second.
H: How far the tool backs off after each peck.
C: How close the rapid comes to the last peck.
R: Drilling: peck factor. Tapping: R0 clutch tapping (default), R1 rigid tapping.

G84.about: Turning from X Z to Q R with an arc whose center is I along X (radius) and K along Z from the start point.

D: Safety distance. D0 or left out: the tool goes back along the profile.
M: Finish stock in Z. Left out, 0.
H: Finish pass feed. None or 0: no finish pass.
F: Feed for the last roughing pass.
I: Arc center along X, from the start point, as a radius.
K: Arc center along Z, from the start point.

G85.about: Facing from X Z to Q R with an arc whose center is I along X (radius) and K along Z from the start point.

D: Safety distance. D0 or left out: the tool goes back along the profile.
M: Finish stock in Z. Left out, 0.
H: Finish pass feed. None or 0: no finish pass.
F: Feed for the last roughing pass.
I: Arc center along X, from the start point, as a radius.
K: Arc center along Z, from the start point.

G86.about: Threading along Z from X Z to Q R, depth I in passes of B, pitch C. The signs of I and B give the direction and the infeed. The tool ends at the approach point and G40 is active after the cycle.

K: Z where the thread is measured, for thread repair.
D: Safety distance the tool pulls back.
W: With K: spindle angle at the point where the thread is measured, for thread repair.

G87.about: Threading on the face from X Z to Q R, depth I in passes of B, pitch C. The signs of I and B give the direction and the infeed. The tool ends at the approach point and G40 is active after the cycle.

K: X where the thread is measured, for thread repair. The manuals contradict each other: the canned cycles manual says Z, the quick reference X. X fits a face thread, whose Z doesn't change along the thread.
D: Safety distance the tool pulls back.
W: With K: spindle angle at the point where the thread is measured, for thread repair.

G88.about: Grooving along X. G40 is active after the cycle.

D: Safety distance the tool pulls back.
K: Dwell at the bottom, in hundredths of a second.

G89.about: Grooving along Z. G40 is active after the cycle.

D: Safety distance the tool pulls back.
K: Dwell at the bottom, in hundredths of a second.

G160.about: Live tool drilling or tapping on the face at J points from angle Q. The main spindle is stopped. In G95 the cycle needs a G94 feed programmed before. The tool ends at the approach point and G40 is active after the cycle.

D: Safety distance the tool pulls back.
K: Dwell at the bottom, in hundredths of a second.
H: How far the tool backs off after each peck.
C: How close the rapid comes to the last peck.
R: Drilling: peck factor. Tapping: R0 clutch tapping (default), R1 rigid tapping.
Q: Spindle angle of the first hole.
J: Number of holes, counting the first.
S: Live tool speed in rpm; the sign gives the direction. Left out, the live tool doesn't start.
N: Number of the live tool spindle.

G161.about: Live tool drilling or tapping on the side at J points from angle Q. The main spindle is stopped. In G95 the cycle needs a G94 feed programmed before. The tool ends at the approach point and G40 is active after the cycle.

D: Safety distance the tool pulls back.
K: Dwell at the bottom, in hundredths of a second.
H: How far the tool backs off after each peck.
C: How close the rapid comes to the last peck.
R: Drilling: peck factor. Tapping: R0 clutch tapping (default), R1 rigid tapping.
Q: Spindle angle of the first hole.
J: Number of holes, counting the first.
S: Live tool speed in rpm; the sign gives the direction. Left out, the live tool doesn't start.
N: Number of the live tool spindle.

G162.about: Live tool slot along Z on the side, J slots from angle Q. F is the slot feed; the feed from before the cycle stays active afterwards. In G95 the cycle needs a G94 feed programmed before. G40 is active after the cycle.

Q: Spindle angle of the first slot.
J: Number of slots, counting the first.
S: Live tool speed in rpm; the sign gives the direction. Left out, the live tool doesn't start.
N: Number of the live tool spindle.
D: Safety distance the tool pulls back.
F: Feed along the slot. Doesn't replace the active feed.

G163.about: Live tool slot along X on the face, J slots from angle Q. F is the slot feed; the feed from before the cycle stays active afterwards. In G95 the cycle needs a G94 feed programmed before. G40 is active after the cycle.

Q: Spindle angle of the first slot.
J: Number of slots, counting the first.
S: Live tool speed in rpm; the sign gives the direction. Left out, the live tool doesn't start.
N: Number of the live tool spindle.
D: Safety distance the tool pulls back.
F: Feed along the slot. Doesn't replace the active feed.

X: Hole position in X. After this line, every move drills another hole, until G80.
Z: Reference plane: where the feed starts. G99 comes back up to it between holes, G98 to where the tool was.
I: Depth of the hole (absolute in G90; from the reference plane in G91).
K: Dwell at the bottom, in seconds.
A: Spindle on the way out: A0 keeps it turning, A1 stops it.

G81.about: Fagor drilling: rapid to the reference plane Z, feed to the depth I, dwell K, rapid back out.

G82.about: Drilling with a peck that changes: the first peck is B, each later one R times the last, never less than L.

D: Distance from the reference plane to the surface.
H: How far the tool backs off after each peck.
C: How close the rapid comes to the last peck.
J: Go back to the reference plane every J pecks.
R: Peck factor: each peck is R times the last.

G83.about: Deep-hole drilling with a constant peck: J pecks of I each.

I: Depth of each peck (not the total depth).

G84.about: Tapping to depth I. R0 is normal tapping, R1 rigid tapping, where J, B and H also apply.

R: R0 normal tapping, R1 rigid tapping.
J: Rigid tapping: the way out runs J times the tapping feed.
B: Rigid tapping: depth of each step, for chip breaking.
H: Rigid tapping: how far the tool backs off after each step.

G85.about: Reaming: feed in to the depth I, dwell K, feed back out.

G86.about: Boring to depth I. R picks the way out: R0 rapid with the spindle stopped, R1 at the feed rate.

R: Way out: R0 rapid with the spindle stopped, R1 at the feed rate.
A: Spindle: A0 in turning and out stopped, A1 in stopped and out turning.
D: Clearance along the first axis of the plane.
E: Clearance along the second axis of the plane.

G87.about: Rectangular pocket: half length J, half width K, passes of B down to I, finishing stock L.

J: Half the pocket's length; the sign gives the direction.
D: Distance from the reference plane to the surface.
A: Angle of the pocket to the first axis.
M: Corners: M0 square, M1 rounded, M2 chamfered.

G88.about: Circular pocket of radius J, passes of B down to I, finishing stock L.

J: Pocket radius; the sign gives the direction.
D: Distance from the reference plane to the surface.

G210.about: Bore milling: mills a hole of diameter J down to depth I in a helix of step B.

J: Hole diameter; the sign gives the direction.
K: Diameter of the hole already there.
B: Helix step; positive also mills the bottom.

G211.about: Inside thread milling: thread diameter J, thread depth K, pitch B.

J: Thread diameter; the sign gives the direction.
B: Thread pitch; positive mills from the surface down.
C: C0 one pass, C1 single-edge cutter, or the number of cutter edges.

G212.about: Outside thread milling: thread diameter J, thread depth K, pitch B.

J: Thread diameter; the sign gives the direction.
B: Thread pitch; positive mills from the surface down.
C: C0 one pass, C1 single-edge cutter, or the number of cutter edges.
